title: Paloma Security Operations: Locks on a Personal Sender Account and Their Release
content:
Paloma security locks an active Personal Sender Account for one of four reasons:

| Lock reason | When it is placed |
|---|---|
| failed sign-ins | after the level's number of consecutive failed sign-ins |
| password-reset abuse | after repeated password-reset requests |
| device-change review | when a sign-in from a new device fails its review |
| suspected takeover | on signs of account takeover |

## Self-release

A failed-sign-ins lock releases itself the level's self-release time in minutes after the moment the lock was placed, when that figure is above 0.

## Release by a support agent

A support agent may release a lock only when all of the following hold:

1. **Caller verified on this call.** The caller passes identity verification on this call, shown by an identity verification record for the customer marked verified.
2. **Releasable reason.** The lock reason is one of the current level's agent-releasable lock reasons.
3. **Government ID, where the level requires it.** When the level requires an ID document for an agent release, a government ID whose latest review is accepted and whose expiry date is later than the unlock date is on file.

A suspected-takeover lock, and any lock whose reason is not among the level's agent-releasable reasons, is released only by Paloma Fraud Operations after its own review, and the agent does not release it.

## Effect of a release

Releasing a lock clears the lock reason and the moment it was placed, returns the account to active, and never changes the level, the limits or any transfer.

## Hypothetical cases

- An account at Paloma Premier is locked for a device-change review. That reason is not agent-releasable at Paloma Premier, so the agent does not release it.
- An account at Paloma Verified Plus is locked for failed sign-ins, and the caller passes identity verification on the call. The agent may release it only if a government ID whose latest review is accepted and whose expiry date is later than the unlock date is on file, because Paloma Verified Plus requires one for an agent release.
- A government ID that expires on the unlock date itself does not meet condition 3: its expiry date must be later than the unlock date.
